bib.title: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch), Appendix A: Introduction to PyTorch

question: What PyTorch fundamentals (tensors, autograd, nn.Module, data loaders, training loop, GPU and DDP use) does a reader need to implement LLMs from scratch?
contributions: A primer on PyTorch tensors, autograd, multilayer networks, Dataset/DataLoader, a training loop, model saving, single-GPU and DDP training, using a toy 2-feature 2-class dataset.

limits: Primer only; explicitly not exhaustive coverage of PyTorch.
Toy 5-example dataset: no measured speedups, no real training; GPU speedup is asserted not measured (A.9.2 'we probably won't see a speedup').
Pinned to PyTorch 2.4.0; DDP outputs shown with PyTorch 2.2.1+cu117.
Multi-GPU section marked not required for the book.
practices: Subclass torch.nn.Module; define layers in __init__ and the computation in forward (A.5).
Return logits from the model and let the loss function (cross_entropy) apply softmax internally, for numerical stability (A.5, A.7).
Use torch.no_grad() for inference to save memory and compute (A.5).
Call optimizer.zero_grad() each update to avoid gradient accumulation (A.7).
Call model.train() and model.eval() even when no dropout/batchnorm is present (A.7).
Seed with torch.manual_seed for reproducible init and shuffling (A.5, A.6).
Shuffle training loader, not test loader; set drop_last=True to avoid a much smaller last batch (A.6).
Use a validation set for hyperparameter tuning and the test set once (A.7).
Write device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu') so code runs on CPU too (A.9.2).
Save and load via state_dict; the architecture must match exactly (A.8).
Use DDP with DistributedSampler, one process per GPU, NCCL backend; run as a script not in Jupyter (A.9.3).
Guard prints with rank == 0 in DDP (A.9.3).
Use Python one or two releases older than latest when installing PyTorch (A.1.3).

optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.5)
for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    model.train()
    for batch_idx, (features, labels) in enumerate(train_loader):
        logits = model(features)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, labels)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
